parameter_notes.L: Screw lead. Confirmed actual system value: 2 mm/rev (updated 2026-09-02; supersedes the earlier 1 mm/rev assumption).
parameter_notes.N_r: Rotor teeth. Given. Source: 1.8 deg step angle.
parameter_notes.T_hold: Holding torque. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 model_parameters.json 'holding_torque'.
parameter_notes.T_d: Detent torque amplitude. Confirmed actual system value: 5e-3 N*m (5 mN*m), updated 2026-09-02; supersedes the earlier 3e-3 N*m value.
parameter_notes.I_m: Rotor inertia. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'J_m'.
parameter_notes.I_c: Coupling inertia. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'J_c'.
parameter_notes.I_s: Screw rotational inertia. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Computed as a solid-cylinder estimate (0.5*m*r^2) from Rev 3 screw geometry (density 7850 kg/m^3, diameter 8mm, length 192mm) since no I_s value exists anywhere in the workspace.
parameter_notes.I_sb: Support bearing inner ring inertia. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc, no reference value found anywhere in the workspace. Order-of-magnitude guess, smaller than I_s.
parameter_notes.M_screw: Screw axial mass. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Same solid-cylinder estimate used for I_s.
parameter_notes.M_s: Nut and stage mass. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Sum of Rev 3 'nut_mass' + 'stage_mass' (this reduced model lumps nut and stage into one axial coordinate x_n).
parameter_notes.k_c: Coupling torsional stiffness. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'k_c_series'.
parameter_notes.k_s1: Screw torsional stiffness, motor side. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'k_theta_a'.
parameter_notes.k_s2: Screw torsional stiffness, bearing side. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'k_theta_b'.
parameter_notes.k_nut: Screw-nut axial contact stiffness. PLACEHOLDER, TBD in source doc. Reused from Rev 3 'k_mnt'. As of the recoupled model (2026-08-17 update) this enters K/C directly as a reflected coupling between theta_s and the axial coordinates via L/2*pi, replacing the earlier T_fric,nut friction port.
parameter_notes.k_brg: Support bearing axial stiffness. Source doc gives an explicit range of 7.5e6 to 15.3e6 N/m (Barden duplex, light preload); this value is the midpoint of that range, not from Rev 3.
parameter_notes.c_c: Coupling torsional damping. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Assumed 2% of critical damping against k_c and the I_m/I_c reduced inertia.
parameter_notes.c_s1: Screw torsional damping, motor side. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Assumed 2% of critical damping against k_s1 and the I_c/I_s reduced inertia.
parameter_notes.c_s2: Screw torsional damping, bearing side. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Assumed 2% of critical damping against k_s2 and the I_s/I_sb reduced inertia.
parameter_notes.c_nut: Screw-nut axial damping. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Assumed 2% of critical damping against k_nut and the M_screw/M_s reduced mass. As of the recoupled model (2026-08-17 update) this enters K/C directly, replacing the earlier T_fric,nut friction port.
parameter_notes.c_brg: Support bearing axial damping. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Assumed 2% of critical damping against k_brg and M_screw (grounded spring).
parameter_notes.c_EM: Electromagnetic (rotor) damping, C[0,0] += c_EM (Sec 3.1/5.4). PLACEHOLDER. As of the 2026-08-18 update this IS applied by default (not optional): mode 1 (176.7 Hz, the whole rotational chain moving nearly rigidly against k_EM) barely engages c_c, c_s1, c_s2 as a damping path and came out at zeta=4.9e-5 without it -- a ~74s settling time, impractical for the stepping simulation. Value is bisected (not the 10%-of-critical guess used previously) to hit exactly zeta=0.02 on mode 1; it barely disturbs modes 2-6 (already near 2% from the other c_* placeholders). Implemented as plain viscous damping of theta_m against a fixed frame only -- the paired theta_dot_cmd feedforward column in Sec 5.4's literal variant is intentionally omitted because theta_cmd is a staircase and its derivative is a train of Dirac impulses, ill-posed for lsim on a finite grid.
